subject: Preflight: traffic mirroring & fallback exercise for VPC/on-prem cutover
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference.com>

Cc: ops@networks.example.com
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Preflight exercise: traffic mirroring + fallback (weekend window)

Team —

We need to run a controlled preflight for the Acme Financial VPC/on-prem cutover next Thursday. Goal: validate our traffic-mirroring pipeline, failover to hosted fallback, and confirm there are no request-level regressions in latency or errors. This is the checklist I'm proposing (attach: preflight-checklist-v2.pdf):

- Mirror 5% of production traffic to the on‑prem canary (2 AZs) for 30m.
- Run BGP flap simulation on the edge router (vendor to coordinate).
- Evict one k8s node in each canary cluster during the mirror window and monitor KV cache warmup.
- Exercise rollback: force routing to hosted fallback, validate session continuity for streaming responses.
- Capture latency histograms (p50/p95/p99), and token-level error rates.

Can Connor and Marissa own the mirror and warmup steps? Laura, will you own the observability gating (dashboards, alerts)? I've looped in NetworkOps (ops@networks.example.com) for BGP and iptables-level tests.

Timing proposal: Thu 2027-04-29 02:00–03:30 UTC (low traffic). I recommend we run a dry run Tue 2027-04-27 22:00–22:30 UTC to validate playbook commands and smoke probes.

If no objections, I'll send the calendar invites and runbook links.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Preflight exercise: traffic mirroring + fallback (weekend window)

Rishi —

Happy to own the mirror and node-eviction steps. Quick notes from infra:

- Mirror will be implemented using our sidecar duplication path (rate-limiter on edge). I’ll set it to 5% as suggested; can toggle to 2–10% during dry run.
- For node eviction, we'll use a graceful cordon+drain followed by a forced eviction for the second iteration to test KV cache rebuild. Expect ~10–20s of extra latency during warmup for affected keys.
- I ran a quick netdiag against the customer's on-prem egress (see netdiag-output-20270427.txt) — jitter looks fine, but there are two intermediate hops with packet loss spikes (0.4–0.6%) during a 5m window. Ops vendor should review before the dry run.

Marissa, can you own the canary cluster scaling policy so we don't hit quota during the mirror?

Connor
Staff SRE
Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-04-28T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Post-dry-run readout: mirror & fallback validation (notes + next steps)

Team / Alex —

Thanks for running the dry run tonight — this thread is the consolidated readout. Summary below (mirror window Tue 2027-04-27 22:00–22:25 UTC):

What we ran:
- 2% mirror traffic to on-prem canary (10m steady + 5m ramp) using sidecar duplication.
- BGP controlled flap (single prefix) performed by vendor; logs attached.
- Single node graceful eviction in canary cluster; forced eviction replayed once.
- Streaming harness validated session reattach for 2m streams.

Observations / findings:
- Latency: mirrored p95 increased by ~85ms during forced eviction warmup; p50 unchanged. No request-level 5xx observed from mirror path.
- Packet loss spikes correlate with two intermediate hops (matches Connor's netdiag). Vendor to re-home one transiting link; suggested mitigation: increase TCP retransmit threshold in sidecar to 200ms to avoid transient errors.
- Mirror header (X-Redwood-Mirror) validated by Acme telemetry; they will filter for analytics/billing.
- During fallback switch test we observed one streaming session fail to reattach (1 of 120 attempts). Investigation points to a race where session metadata wasn't replicated to fallback quickly enough — SRE follow-up required.
- No data retention leaks observed in a cursory check; security wants a one-line confirmation in the production runbook that mirrored payloads are discarded within 5 minutes in the mirror tier.

Action items (owners):
- Vendor: remediate transiting link and provide post-fix netdiag (ops@networks.example.com) — due 2027-04-29 14:00 UTC.
- Connor: add second warmup pass and increase sidecar retransmit threshold to 200ms for main cutover. Update mirror toggle script. (due 2027-04-29 09:00 UTC)
- Laura: add gating on streaming reattach success (>=99.5%) and a short security confirmation line in the runbook. (due 2027-04-29 12:00 UTC)
- Rishi: schedule final short overlap Wed 2027-04-28 01:00 UTC and main cutover Thu 2027-04-29 02:00–03:30 UTC; send invites after owners ack.

Final note: the dry run exposed a small edge case but nothing blocking. Recommend proceeding with the overlap sanity check Wed and main preflight Thurs after the vendor netdiag is confirmed.

I'll attach the vendor logs and the updated playbook shortly.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
